what_this_is: One real issuance run over runs/gate0-linux-container-fault/, retained as a measurement record.
revision_note: The retained container run was produced at 0d281c03, not at this worktree's HEAD. Verification therefore used the run's own revision as expected_source_revision. Under a true exact-head policy every row would additionally carry fault.stale-revision and the matrix fault.matrix-stale-revision. Closing Gate 0 on this axis requires re-running the driver at the exact head being claimed.

key_provenance.origin: secrets.token_hex(32), generated inside the measuring shell
key_provenance.consequence: The key was never written to disk and no longer exists. The retained bundle is therefore NOT re-verifiable by anyone and must never be mistaken for production trust. It records that the boundary worked, nothing more.
key_provenance.owner_action_required: Production issuer keys and the issuer-to-authority policy are owner-provisioned. Nothing in this repository provisions them.

what_changed: Only the authenticity question. All nine retained Linux-host observations entered the trust set; every substantive blocker stayed exactly where it was. Two failed rows, four rows blocked on an unavailable Docker CLI, and fifteen rows with no observation at all remain open.
what_did_not_change: Signing an observation grants authenticity, never a verdict. The two failed and four blocked rows were attested and still block.
remaining_for_a_whole-matrix_verdict: The fifteen fault.missing rows are thirteen deterministic-fixture rows and two live-runtime rows. No collector emits RuntimeFaultObservation records for either authority; the deterministic-fixture rows name pytest node ids in scenario.executor but nothing maps a pytest result to an observation.

daedalus/gates/fault_matrix.py is a separate manifest/receipt subsystem with its own verdict and does not feed daedalus/runtimes/fault_matrix.py. The Windows-side pass count comes from that other path and is not currently merged into this matrix.
The four Docker-blocked rows need a run on a host with a reachable Linux Docker engine.
Both remaining columns need their own issuer identity and authority policy before their observations can be trusted.
